SPECIFICATION FOR 
ACCOMMODATION LADDERS 

PART 1 UP TO 7 m LENGTH 



1. Scope — Covers accommodation ladders up to 7 m length used on merchant ships (excluding 
passenger ships ) to enable persons to embark and disembark safely. 

2. Terminology 

2.1 Nominal Length L t — For a single-flight ladder, the distance from the centre of the top pin to the 
centre of the lower platform holding pin. 

2.2 Design Length L t — - The maximum distance between supporting points ( see Fig. 1 ). 

2.3 Width W— The minimum effective width of the walking surface between hand/guard rails ( see 
Fig. 2 ). 

2.4 Handrail Heights — The vertical height of the upper surface of the handrail, measured form the 
highest point of the standing surface presented by the steps when the ladder is at its minimum angle 
of use (see Fig. 2 ). 

3. Fixed Platform Ladder 

3.1 The ladder is hinged from a fixed anchorage, and is capable of being varied in inclination between 
the ship and the lower access level. 

3.2 The ladder is supported by steel wire ropes or chains from suspension point(s) in the lower part 
of the ladder. 

4. Materials 

4.1 The principal side members of the ladder shall be constructed from steel conforming to 
IS : 226-1975 'Specification for structural steel standard quality ( first revision )' or aluminium alloy 
conforming to Grade 5300 of IS : 737-1974 'Specification for wrought aluminium alloys, sheet and 
strip ( for generel engineering purposes )'. 

Alternative 

5. Dimensions 

5.1 Nominal Length L x — The range of nominal lengths shall be 50 to 70 m in 0*5 m increments. 

5.2 Width W — Shall be 600 or 750 mm for all ladders up to 70 m length. 

5.3 Distance Between Steps — When measured along the line tangential to the step noses, shall be 
300 mm. 

5.4 Top Handrail Height, H — Shall be not less than 1 000 mm. An intermediate rail at mid-height 
shall be provided ( see Fig. 2 ). 

5.4.1 A canvas or equivalent protection should be arranged from middle rail to bottom end for safety 
of children. 

6. Design 

6.1 Minimum Angle of Use — Ladders shall be designed for safe operation in a horizontal position. 

6.2 Max/mum Angle of Use — With the steps horizontal, the ladder shall operate safely up to an 
angle of 55° from the horizontal. 

6.3 Design Loading — The ladders shall be designed to support a uniform load equivalent to 735 N 
on every step when the ladder is in horizontal position. 

6.4 Step Design — Individual steps shall be designed to withstand a central point load of 735 N.

IS: 10943 ( Parti ) -1984 

6.5 Design Loading for Access and intermediate Platforms— The platforms shall be designed to support 
a uniform loading of 4 000 N/m. The framework and supporting structure of the upper platforms shall 
in addition be designed to carry the weight of the suspended ladder together with the design load 
given in 6.3. 

6.6 Design Loading for Handrail — Handrails and supports shall be designed for a side loading at the 
upper handrail of 500 N/m without permanent deformation. 

6.7 Safety Factor — The allowable stress used in the design of the ladder, with loading specified in 6.3, 
shall be determined by applying a safety factor of 5 for steel and 3 for aluminium. 

7. Construction 

7.1 The ladder is used ordinarily at an inclination up to 55° against horizontal, its construction, 
however, shall be allowed to use also at the inclination of 65°. The lower platform shall be constructed 
so as it can be fixed to suit angle of ladder used ( see Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 ). 

7.2 Contact surfaces of aluminium alloy and steel shall be painted and insulated properly to prevent 
electrolytic corrosion. 

7 3 All steel parts shall be galvanized as given in IS : 4759-1979 'Specification for hot-dip zinc 
coatings on structural steel and other allied products ( first revision )*. 

7.4 The handrail shall be of handy shape and size, and when a rope is used for a handrail, it shall be 
fibre rope of 22 mm outside diameter covered with plastics or nylon rope covered with PVC or aluminium 
wire rope. 

7.5 The surface of step shall be of non skid type achieved with half punching the steps or with welded 
strips or any other suitable methods. 

7.6 Side roller is an optional item. 

8. Testing 

8.1 Procedure 

8.1 .1 Each ladder shall be tested in a horizontal position, simply supported at the ends of the design 
length L% ( see Fig. 3 ), to prove the longitudinal strength and to measure maximum deflection. 

8.1.2 The ladder and platform shall be uniformly loaded with a load equivalent to 735 N on every 
step. 

8.2 Measurement and Examination 

8.2.1 The maximum deflection of a ladder when loaded shall not exceed. 

'q- for steel and ■ * Q for aluminium 

8.2.2 After removal of the test load, the ladder shall be carefully examined to ensure that there are 
no signs of failure of the structure and that no permanent deformation has taken place. 

9. Designation 

9.1 The ladder shall be designated by title and nominal length. 

10. Marking 

10.1 The following information shall be marked on readily visible place on the ladder body: 

a) Nominal length (m), 

b) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, and 

c) Date of manufacture and testing. 

10.2 iSI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution.
